items.title: Sheaf and limit preserving properties of the functors of points where a module map is injective, surjective, bijective or zero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the four functors recording that a module map becomes injective, surjective, bijective or zero satisfy the fpqc sheaf property, and that the surjectivity, vanishing and bijectivity functors are limit preserving under the stated finiteness hypotheses (statement lines 5918-5931, tag 05MJ). The sheaf part is a short faithful flatness argument on stalks, but the limit preserving parts require a real reduction each: the quasi-compact source is covered by finitely many affine opens mapping into affine opens of the base, the question is turned into one about a module map over a directed colimit of algebras, and the three cases are then matched to the corresponding algebraic colimit statements. The reduction scheme is uniform but must be carried out three times with the right finiteness hypothesis each time, so the claim is H2.
